best_for: Players who own GameCube and Wii discs and want to play them on a 64-bit PC or Mac with a reasonably fast CPU and GPU.

points.title: GameCube and Wii on one emulator
points.text: Dolphin runs games for both consoles. It reads common disc image formats, including ISO, GCZ, CISO, WBFS, WIA and RVZ.

points.title: Bring your own games
points.text: Dolphin ships no games. The FAQ says downloading commercial games is illegal, even ones you bought, and suggests dumping your own discs with a homebrewed Wii and CleanRip.

points.title: Speed beats core count
points.text: Dolphin depends on clock speed and per-core performance more than on many cores. The GPU needs DirectX 11.1 and OpenGL 4.4, and 2 GB of RAM or more is recommended. Only 64-bit systems are supported.

points.title: Windows here is an old release
points.text: The Windows entry on this site is version 5.0. The project now numbers releases by year and month, such as 2609 for September 2026 and its hotfix 2609b, and offers them for Windows x64 and Arm64 on its download page. Windows builds need the 64-bit Visual C++ redistributable.

points.title: Releases or development builds
points.text: Releases come every few months and are the stable choice. Development builds appear after each code change and are less tested, but get fixes first.

points.title: Mac and Linux
points.text: The Mac build is universal for Apple silicon and Intel and needs macOS 11 or later. On Linux, the Flatpak here is not verified on Flathub, so it is a community package rather than one from the Dolphin team.

points.title: One version per platform
points.text: Each platform lists only one version here, so a downgrade needs another source, such as the release list on the Dolphin site.
